title: Coproduct module sheaves as locally finite-coordinate tuples
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] whose topology is given by covering families, with fibre products of objects, and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on it. Assume the sheafification of presheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules exists [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Let $I$ be a set in the fixed sheaf universe and $(H_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Form the sectionwise product $P=\prod_{i\in I}H_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Define a subpresheaf $S\subseteq P$ by
$$S(V)=\{(h_i)_i\in P(V):\ \text{there is a covering }\{V_a\to V\}_a\text{ and finite }B_a\subseteq I\text{ with }h_i|_{V_a}=0\text{ for }i\notin B_a\}.$$
Restrictions and module operations are induced from $P$. Then $S$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules. For each $i$, the coordinate insertion $\iota_i:H_i\to P$ factors through $S$, and these maps make $S$ a coproduct of the $H_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $T$, composition with the $\iota_i$ is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(S,T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i\in I}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(H_i,T).$$
Consequently the canonical map $\bigoplus_{i\in I}H_i\to\prod_{i\in I}H_i$ is a monomorphism and its image is exactly this subsheaf $S$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits and its proof (module-sheaf coproduct is the sheafification of the sectionwise coproduct); explicit image in the sectionwise product.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise] to the discrete diagram on $I$. Its sectionwise limit is the sheaf $P$, with $P(V)=\prod_i H_i(V)$ and coordinatewise restrictions and module operations. The diagram is small because $I$ belongs to the fixed sheaf universe.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, limits paragraph; Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2)

proof.text: Check the subpresheaf and submodule assertions directly. If $h\in S(V)$ is witnessed by $\{V_a\to V\}$ and $B_a$, then along $W\to V$ its restriction is witnessed by the pulled-back covering $\{W\times_VV_a\to W\}$ with the same finite sets. The zero tuple is witnessed by the identity covering with empty support. Negation and multiplication by $r\in\mathcal O(V)$ preserve each witness. For $h,k\in S(V)$ with witnesses $(V_a,B_a)$ and $(W_b,C_b)$, base change followed by composition gives the covering $\{V_a\times_VW_b\to V\}_{a,b}$, on which $h+k$ vanishes outside $B_a\cup C_b$. Thus each $S(V)$ is a submodule of $P(V)$, and its restrictions are the inherited semilinear maps. Functoriality and the module identities hold because they hold coordinatewise in $P$.

source.place: Tag 03CW, definition-sheaf-modules; agent calculation using Sites Tag 00VH, definition-site (base change and composition of coverings)

proof.text: For a covering $\{V_a\to V\}$ and a matching family $h^a\in S(V_a)$, its image in $P$ has a unique glued section $h\in P(V)$. For each $a$, choose a witnessing covering $\{W_{ab}\to V_a\}_b$ and finite supports $B_{ab}$ for $h^a$. The composite family $\{W_{ab}\to V\}_{a,b}$ is a covering, and $h$ restricts there to tuples vanishing outside $B_{ab}$. Hence $h\in S(V)$. Uniqueness holds since two tuples in $S(V)\subseteq P(V)$ with equal restrictions are equal in the sheaf $P$. This proves the sheaf condition; together with step 2 it makes $S$ a sheaf of modules. This also treats empty covering families, since $P$ has unique gluing for the empty matching family.

source.place: Tag 03CW, definition-sheaf-modules; agent verification of the equalizer condition of Sites Tags 00VM and 00VR

proof.text: For $i\in I$ and $x\in H_i(V)$, let $\iota_{i,V}(x)$ be the tuple with $i$-coordinate $x$ and all other coordinates zero. The identity covering and the finite set $\{i\}$ witness its membership in $S(V)$. Coordinatewise these maps commute with restrictions and are $\mathcal O(V)$-linear, so they define morphisms $\iota_i:H_i\to S$ whose composites with $S\hookrightarrow P$ are the coordinate insertions.

source.place: Tag 03CW, definition-sheaf-modules; agent construction of the coordinate morphisms

proof.text: Fix morphisms $f_i:H_i\to T$, and a section $h\in S(V)$ with witness $(V_a,B_a)$. Put $t_a=\sum_{i\in B_a}f_{i,V_a}(h_i|_{V_a})\in T(V_a)$. On $W=V_a\times_VV_b$, each sum can be enlarged to $B_a\cup B_b$: terms outside its original support are zero, and $f_i(0)=0$. Naturality of $f_i$ then identifies both restricted sums with $\sum_{i\in B_a\cup B_b} f_{i,W}(h_i|_W)$. Thus $(t_a)_a$ is a matching family in $T$ and glues uniquely to a section $f_V(h)\in T(V)$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, coproduct construction; explicit agent finite-sum formula and sheaf gluing, using Tag 03CW

proof.text: The section just defined is independent of the witness. For a second witness $(W_b,C_b)$, use the common refinement $V_a\times_VW_b$. On each of these objects the two prescribed sums coincide after enlargement to $B_a\cup C_b$, exactly as in step 5. Their glued sections therefore agree by separatedness of $T$ on this covering. If a witnessing covering is empty, the same assertion holds since $T(V)$ then has only one section.

source.place: Tag 03CW, definition-sheaf-modules; agent common-refinement and separatedness verification

proof.text: For $q:W\to V$, pull a witness for $h$ back to $W$. The restricted local sum equals the sum constructed for $h|_W$, because $f_i$ commutes with restrictions. Uniqueness of gluing gives $f_W(h|_W)=f_V(h)|_W$. To check additivity, take the common refinement of witnesses for $h$ and $k$ and the union of their finite supports. On each member, the formula of step 5 gives $f(h+k)=\sum_i f_i(h_i+k_i)=\sum_i f_i(h_i)+\sum_i f_i(k_i)$. Separatedness gives additivity on $V$. On a witness for $h$, the same calculation with $r\in\mathcal O(V)$ gives $f(rh)=r f(h)$, since each $f_i$ is linear over the ring of sections on that member. Empty covers are handled by unique gluing. Therefore $f:S\to T$ is a morphism of sheaves of modules.

source.place: Tag 03CW, definition-sheaf-modules; agent verification of naturality and sectionwise linearity of the finite-sum construction

proof.text: For a section $x\in H_i(V)$ use the identity covering and support $\{i\}$ in step 5. Its sum is $f_{i,V}(x)$, so $f\iota_i=f_i$. Conversely, if $g:S\to T$ is a morphism with $g\iota_i=f_i$, then on a witnessing member $V_a$ one has the coordinatewise equality $h|_{V_a}=\sum_{i\in B_a}\iota_i(h_i|_{V_a})$ in $S(V_a)$. Linearity forces $g_V(h)|_{V_a}=t_a$. Uniqueness of gluing forces $g_V(h)=f_V(h)$ for all $V,h$, hence $g=f$. Thus composition with the $\iota_i$ is the displayed bijection. This is the colimit universal property for the discrete diagram on $I$, so $S$ is its coproduct. For $I=\varnothing$, $P$ and $S$ are the zero sheaf and the empty sum formula gives the unique morphism to $T$.

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits, coproduct universal property; explicit agent proof from finite sums and unique gluing

proof.text: Write $Q=\bigoplus_i H_i$ for any chosen coproduct, with maps $\kappa_i$. The universal properties give $u:Q\to S$ and $v:S\to Q$ with $u\kappa_i=\iota_i$ and $v\iota_i=\kappa_i$. Since $uv$ and $vu$ agree with the identity on every coproduct insertion, uniqueness makes them identities. If $m:S\hookrightarrow P$ is the inclusion, the canonical map $c:Q\to P$ satisfies $c\kappa_i=m\iota_i$; hence $c=mu$. The inclusion $m$ is monic: equality after $m$ means equality of all tuples, object by object, and hence equality of the original natural transformations. Since $u$ is invertible, $c$ is monic. Its sectionwise range on every $V$ is $m(S(V))=S(V)$, already a sheaf by step 3. Thus its image subsheaf is exactly $S$ (equivalently, $c$ and $m$ represent the same subobject of $P$).

source.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits; agent universal-property identification and direct cancellation for the image in the product

proof_origin.place: Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits: explicit locally finite-coordinate realization of the sheafified sectionwise coproduct, proved by covers, finite sums and unique gluing
